breadcrumb: Std 9 Social Science (English) — History Unit 7: State and Society in Medieval India — Boxed notes (தெரிந்து தெளிவோம் / Do you know)

questions.quote: Alauddin Khalji (1296–1316 CE) sent military campaigns to the south. The primary objective was to plunder the wealth, rather than to expand his territory. Muhammad Ghori established Muslim rule in Delhi at the end of the 12th century.

en.q: The primary objective of Alauddin Khalji's military campaigns to the south was to:
en.explanation: They aimed at plunder rather than territorial expansion.

ta.q: அலாவுதீன் கில்ஜி தெற்கே நடத்திய படையெடுப்புகளின் முதன்மை நோக்கம் என்ன?
ta.explanation: நிலப்பரப்பை விரிவாக்குவதை விட செல்வத்தைக் கொள்ளையிடுவதே நோக்கம்.

questions.quote: The Bahmani kingdom survived for nearly a century and a half, mainly due to the able administration of Mahmud Gawan. By the end of the fifteenth century, five sultanates came up in the Deccan: Bijapur, Golkonda, Ahmednagar, Berar and Bidar.

en.q: Which of the following was NOT one of the five Deccan sultanates that emerged from the Bahmani kingdom?
en.explanation: The five were Bijapur, Golkonda, Ahmednagar, Berar and Bidar.

ta.q: பாமினி அரசிலிருந்து தோன்றிய ஐந்து தக்காண சுல்தானகங்களுள் இடம்பெறாதது எது?
ta.explanation: பிஜப்பூர், கோல்கொண்டா, அகமதுநகர், பிரார், பிதார் ஆகிய ஐந்து.

questions.quote: Rajendra I took his armies to the Ganges; naval expeditions against Sri Vijaya, Kadaram (Kedah) and Ceylon; title 'gangaiyum kadaramum konda cholan'. Maritime trade expanded; Indic culture spread to south-east Asia, as seen in Angkor Wat.

en.q: Rajendra I earned the title 'Gangaikonda Chola' by taking his armies as far as the:
en.explanation: His title: 'the Chola who had conquered the Ganga and Kadaram'.

ta.q: முதலாம் இராஜேந்திரன் தம் படைகளை எந்த ஆறு வரை கொண்டு சென்றதால் 'கங்கை கொண்ட சோழன்' எனப் பட்டம் பெற்றார்?

questions.quote: The Chola Empire began to decline after the middle of the 13th century. The last known Chola emperor was Rajendra III. The empire died out in 1279 CE. Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan ruled at the end of the 13th century.

en.q: The last known Chola emperor was:
en.explanation: The Chola empire died out in 1279 CE.

questions.quote: Vijayanagar was established by Harihara and Bukka, two brothers, the first rulers of the Sangama dynasty. Capital on the southern banks of the Tungabhadra named Vijayanagara. Harihara crowned in 1336. Dynasties: Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva. Krishnadeva Raya belonged to the Tuluva family.

en.q: Arrange the Vijayanagar dynasties in order:
en.explanation: Harihara and Bukka founded the Sangama dynasty, followed by the Saluvas and then the Tuluvas.

ta.explanation: ஹரிஹரர், புக்கரால் சங்கம வம்சம் தொடங்கியது; பின் சாளுவர்; பின் துளுவர்.

questions.quote: After the defeat at Talikota (1565), the Vijayanagar emperors shifted their capital to Penugonda, and eventually to Chandragiri near Tirupati. Babur founded the Mughal empire in 1526 after defeating Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat. Aurangzeb was the last of the great Mughals.

en.q: After the defeat at Talikota, the Vijayanagar capital was shifted first to:
en.explanation: Then eventually to Chandragiri near Tirupati.

ta.q: தலைக்கோட்டைத் தோல்விக்குப் பின் விஜயநகரத் தலைநகர் முதலில் எங்கு மாற்றப்பட்டது?
ta.explanation: பின்னர் இறுதியாக திருப்பதி அருகே சந்திரகிரிக்கு மாறியது.

questions.quote: Chola period: the basic unit of local administration was the village (ur), followed by the sub-region (nadu) and district (kottam). Tax-free villages granted to Brahmins were known as brahmadeya. Marketing centres and towns were known as nagaram. Each had its own assembly.

en.q: In Chola administration, tax-free villages granted to Brahmins were called:
en.explanation: Nagaram were marketing centres and towns; nadu a sub-region.

ta.q: சோழர் நிர்வாகத்தில் பிராமணர்களுக்கு வரி விலக்குடன் வழங்கப்பட்ட கிராமங்கள் எவ்வாறு அழைக்கப்பட்டன?

questions.quote: Al-Beruni, Ibn Batuta and Ferishta are among the best known Muslim historians of the medieval period. Deccan sultanates of Bijapur and Golkonda were broad-minded and secular in outlook.

en.q: Which of the following was NOT a Muslim historian/traveller of the medieval period mentioned in the text?
en.explanation: Megasthenes was a Greek envoy in the Mauryan period.

ta.q: பாடநூல் குறிப்பிடும் இடைக்கால முஸ்லிம் வரலாற்றாசிரியர்களுள் இடம்பெறாதவர் யார்?

questions.quote: St Francis Xavier made the fishing community take to Christianity in the Tuticorin region. Roberto de Nobili, a scholar, was based in Madurai. Guru Nanak founded Sikhism. The Parsis settled in Gujarat; the Jews lived in Kerala.

en.q: The Jesuit scholar based in Madurai was:
en.explanation: St Francis Xavier worked among the fishing community of the Tuticorin region.

questions.quote: Kamban's Ramayana was presented in the temple at Srirangam; Sekkilar's Periyapuranam at the temple in Chidambaram. Kalingattup-parani and Muvarula are other great works. Bronze images by the 'lost wax' process; Nataraja.

en.q: Sekkilar's Periyapuranam was presented (arangetram) at the temple in:
en.explanation: Kamban's Ramayana was presented at Srirangam.

questions.quote: Tansen is well known in the performing arts under Akbar. Mughals constructed Shahjahanabad (Delhi) and Fatehpur Sikri. Mughal miniatures were book illustrations. Venkatamakhi codified the ragas of Carnatic music. A new style of Tamil literature called Prabandham emerged under Vijayanagar.

en.q: The Carnatic musicologist who codified the ragas during the Vijayanagar–Nayak period was:
en.explanation: Venkatamakhi, son of Govinda Dikshitar, codified ragas; Tansen was in Akbar's court.

ta.q: விஜயநகர-நாயக்கர் காலத்தில் கர்நாடக இசையின் ராகங்களை வகைப்படுத்தியவர் யார்?
ta.explanation: கோவிந்த தீட்சிதரின் மகன் வேங்கடமகி ராகங்களை வகுத்தார்.

questions.quote: Maize and tobacco were two new crops introduced after the arrival of the Europeans. Papaya, pineapple, guava and cashew nut came from America. Potatoes, chillies and tomatoes also became integral to Indian food.

en.q: Which of the following was a new crop introduced after the arrival of the Europeans?
en.explanation: Maize and tobacco were new crops; sugarcane, cotton and indigo were already grown.

ta.q: ஐரோப்பியர் வருகைக்குப் பின் அறிமுகமான புதிய பயிர் எது?
ta.explanation: மக்காச்சோளம், புகையிலை புதியவை; கரும்பு, பருத்தி, அவுரி முன்பே பயிரிடப்பட்டன.

questions.quote: Textiles accounted for nearly 90 per cent of the total exports from India. Diamonds were then found only in India. Silk, drugs, dye woods and sugar from Persia; gold, ivory and slaves from east Africa.

en.q: According to the textbook, what share of India's total exports did textiles account for in the medieval period?
en.explanation: Textiles were nearly 90% of exports; India was also the only source of diamonds.

ta.q: பாடநூலின்படி, இடைக்கால இந்தியாவின் மொத்த ஏற்றுமதியில் துணிகளின் பங்கு எவ்வளவு?
ta.explanation: ஏற்றுமதியில் ஏறத்தாழ 90% துணிகள்; வைரம் இந்தியாவில் மட்டுமே கிடைத்தது.

questions.quote: Holy Roman Empire: Charlemagne, king of Franks, first Holy Roman Emperor (800 CE). King John of England forced to sign Magna Carta in 1215. King John was a contemporary of Sultan Iltutmish.

en.q: The Magna Carta, the Charter of Liberty, was signed by King John of England in:
en.explanation: The nobles forced King John to sign it; he was a contemporary of Sultan Iltutmish.

ta.q: இங்கிலாந்து மன்னர் ஜான் 'மேக்னா கார்ட்டா' உரிமைச் சாசனத்தில் எப்போது கையெழுத்திட்டார்?
ta.explanation: பிரபுக்கள் கட்டாயப்படுத்தியதால் கையெழுத்திட்டார்; இவர் இல்துத்மிஷின் சமகாலத்தவர்.
